content:
Earlier this year, the PC market was caught off guard by Apple's launch of the MacBook Neo. Although the laptop's aggressive pricing strategy has had to be adjusted in response to market conditions, it took several months before Windows-based rivals announced their own competing products. Today it's HP's turn, unveiling a brand-new laptop equipped with an OLED display, also starting at US$699 — though that comes with quite a few strings attached.

The HP OmniBook 5 14 looks like a fusion of the MacBook Neo's colourful yet affordable chassis and the more refined, understated green and blue tones of the Apple iPad Air lineup. The body is just 11.77mm thick, and the 14-inch model weighs only 2.56 pounds — seemingly ideal for the just-passed back-to-school shopping season. The real star, however, is that 14-inch display: HP has swapped the IPS panel typically found at this price point for an OLED one, offering two OLED options — more on that later. On either side of the chassis are two "full-function" USB-C ports and a headphone jack, and when you open the lid, an FHD camera with Windows Hello support greets you.

On the specs side, HP says it supports up to an Intel Core 7 processor, but the unit currently on show only has that option. Battery life looks impressive on paper — up to 42 hours of local video playback, though the battery capacity isn't stated — but admittedly, local video playback tests don't always reflect real-world usage. HP says the laptop is compatible with its 65W GaN mini charger, which is expected to ship in the box. Beyond that, the known specs include dual microphones and a speaker system tuned by "Poly Studio." If you feel there's still a lot left unannounced, you're not alone.

For one thing, it's unclear what processor the US$700 version uses, making a direct comparison with Apple's A18 Pro difficult. HP has likewise chosen to omit storage and memory configurations entirely — not even the "maximum" configuration is mentioned — a reflection of the pressure the PC market is under amid the current RAM shortage. Even the laptop's biggest selling point comes with a rather awkward caveat: HP spent a great deal of its launch materials hyping the 2.5K OLED display, but that version won't ship until March 2027. The version going on sale at Best Buy later this month will come with a 2K OLED display, with peak brightness dropping dramatically from 650 nits to just 300 nits.

Although there are still plenty of unanswered questions — and some of the answers are underwhelming — if you're still interested in HP's offering, stay tuned for more details to be released before it hits retail shelves.
